dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: IFT-12 Block 3 Second Attempt Tonight at 22:30 UTC After May 21 Scrub — Hydraulic Pin Issue Resolved; OLP-2 Inaugural & First Raptor Relight in Space
heroSubtitle: 8,782 days of SpaceX milestones — Starship IFT-12 Block 3 was scrubbed at T-40 seconds on May 21, 2026 when a hydraulic pin on the Mechazilla tower arm failed to retract. Engineers resolved the issue overnight; SpaceX set a second attempt for May 22 at 22:30 UTC (5:30 PM CDT) from Orbital Launch Pad 2 (OLP-2) at Starbase — also the inaugural launch from Pad 2. Booster 19 (33 Raptor 3 engines, 3 grid fins, integrated vented interstage) and Ship 39 V3 (124.4 m, 25% more propellant than V2) remain stacked and ready. Mission objectives: 20 Starlink mass-simulators + 2 heat-shield observer satellites; Booster 19 Gulf of Mexico splashdown; Ship 39 Indian Ocean splashdown; first-ever in-space Raptor relight attempt. No Mechazilla booster catch on this first Block 3 flight; 60–65% favorable weather. IPO context: Binance launched SPCXUSDT pre-IPO perpetual futures on May 21, with crypto markets pricing SpaceX above $2T implied valuation — exceeding the $1.75–2T S-1 range (filed May 20, 2026). Management roadshow targeted week of June 4–8; pricing June 11; Nasdaq (SPCX) listing June 12. SpaceX: 60 orbital missions in 2026, 613 total booster recoveries, 10,427+ Starlink satellites in orbit, 10.3M subscribers.
